items.title: Howie Shear interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2014
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] If you look at some of the — it’s hard to think of a player, a guy like Joe Lovano, they all do other things that come along. [INTERVIEWEE] Oh absolutely. Yeah, yeah, yeah.

ctx.x: And it goes without saying that those studio years, you just have to take care of business. You have to be on time, you can’t have attitude, I mean the whole thing.

The whole thing. Yeah. You have to be on time which means you’ve got to be fairly early. Now if you want to warm up properly if you didn’t get a chance to at home. And then you could look at the music ahead of time, and meet the guys. My favorite thing to do is still playing, even though I like to orchestrate. Because orchestrating and composing is a very lonely life. You sit at home, or if you have an office and there’s no one, it’s eerily quiet and I don’t like that. I like a little chatter. But when you’re a…
I’m a responsible person, so that part doesn’t bother me. But you have to plan. You have to plan.
